candidate.answerReason: The outer prism contains 600 cubic feet, and the open interior occupies 10 × 8 × 4 = 320 cubic feet. Their difference is 280, agreeing with choice B.

methods.label: Subtract the empty interior
methods.explanation:
Each block occupies \(1\) cubic foot, so the number of blocks equals the occupied volume in cubic feet. Imagine filling the empty interior to make a solid rectangular prism. This full prism would contain
\[
12\times10\times5=600
\]
blocks.

The two opposing walls each take one foot from the interior length and width. Thus the empty interior is \(12-2=10\) feet long and \(10-2=8\) feet wide. The top is open, so only the one-foot floor reduces its height, giving \(5-1=4\) feet. The interior would therefore hold
\[
10\times8\times4=320
\]
blocks.

Every position in the full prism is either part of the fort or part of this empty interior. Therefore the fort contains \(600-320=\boxed{280}\) blocks, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses rectangular-prism volume and whole-number subtraction, both appropriate for AMC 8.

methods.label: Count the floor and walls separately
methods.explanation:
Divide the fort into rectangular pieces whose blocks do not overlap. The one-foot-thick floor contains
\[
12\times10\times1=120
\]
blocks. Above the floor, the walls extend another \(5-1=4\) feet.

Count the two long walls at their full length of \(12\) feet, including their corner blocks. Each contains \(12\times1\times4=48\) blocks above the floor. The remaining portions of the two short walls fit between the long walls, so each is \(10-2=8\) feet long and contains \(8\times1\times4=32\) blocks.

The floor is below these wall pieces, and the corners belong only to the long walls, so every block is counted exactly once. The total is
\[
120+2(48)+2(32)=\boxed{280}
\]
blocks, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses an elementary partition into rectangular prisms, with explicit accounting for the shared corners.
